(2) When the branch is selected, the request value under the configured header name is lowercased into email and passed to authenticate_user_by_email; no additional client-credential check is shown between those steps in this crop. (3) If authentication returns a user, that returned user object is passed to create_session_response with set_cookie=True, binding the selected email lookup result to the authenticated session resource. (4) The strongest visible application controls are the password-auth entry gate, configuration and presence of the named header, and the requirement that email authentication produce a user. The accepted policy adds a deployment control not implemented or evidenced by these sources: a trusted reverse proxy must be the sole reachable ingress, remove client-supplied identity headers, and inject the authenticated identity itself. (5) The protected effect is reachable on the source-visible branch where password auth is enabled, the trusted-email-header setting is truthy, the named header is present, and email authentication returns a user. (6) The effective ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH value, configured trusted-email-header name, externally reachable ingress set, proxy stripping/replacement behavior, proxy authentication outcome, and selected-email authentication result can change the deployment answer; none is supplied as an actual deployment observation. (7) The optional provisioning branch checks whether the email already exists and, if absent, invokes signup_handler with that same request-derived email before authenticating by email. Thus it can create the identity that is subsequently looked up, but it does not itself create the session; for an already existing selected user, the visible condition skips provisioning. At most six relevant branch summaries are: password auth disabled blocks with 403; password auth enabled but no trusted-header configuration does not select this shown path; configured branch with the named header absent blocks with 400; header present but authentication producing no user cannot reach the shown session effect; authentication producing a user with policy-compliant ingress prevents an external client from choosing the injected identity under the accepted policy; authentication producing a user with a reachable ingress that preserves a client-supplied identity header would allow that value to select the session identity and would fail the deny expectation. Which deployment branch applies is unknown. Other sign-in modes are expressly omitted and unexamined, as are signup_handler internals, authenticate_user_by_email internals, session-response internals, middleware, proxy configuration, and network topology; the fixed crop is not evidence of repository-wide or all-entry completeness.

facts.statement: The supplied entry is POST /signin, and it checks ENABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH before reaching the trusted-email branch, returning 403 when that gate is false.
The trusted-email branch is selected only when WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER is truthy; within that branch, absence of the configured header name causes a 400 response.
The trusted email, name, groups, and role header names are environment-controlled values; the trusted email header defaults to None when not configured.
The value of the configured trusted-email request header is lowercased and assigned as the email identity used by the branch.
The display name defaults to the request-derived email and may instead come from the optionally configured trusted-name header after URL decoding.
If no user exists for the request-derived email, the branch invokes signup_handler with that same email and generated credentials before attempting email authentication.
The request-derived email is passed to authenticate_user_by_email, and subsequent trusted-header processing is conditioned on that call yielding a user.
The user object produced by email authentication is the user object passed into create_session_response.
When user is truthy, the shown code returns a session response and requests cookie setting; otherwise it returns invalid credentials.
Within the shown trusted-email path, reaching the session effect requires traversal of the password-auth gate, trusted-header branch and header-presence check, followed by a truthy user result.
The supplied source explicitly omits handling for other sign-in modes, so those paths are unexamined in this assessment.
